You need to tell FastAPI about the `/api` prefix with the `--root-path` option. When your app sits behind a proxy that adds a path prefix, you can configure the server with `fastapi run --root-path`.[1]

```console
fastapi run --root-path /api
```

**Why the docs page breaks:** When you open the integrated docs UI (the frontend), it would expect to get the OpenAPI schema at `/openapi.json`[1] instead of the prefixed path. So, the frontend (that runs in the browser) would try to reach `/openapi.json` and wouldn't be able to get the OpenAPI schema.[1]

**Why `--root-path` fixes it:** FastAPI uses this `root_path` to create the default `server` in OpenAPI with the URL provided by `root_path`.[3] You can check the value in a path operation:

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI, Request

app = FastAPI()


@app.get("/app")
def read_main(request: Request):
    return {"message": "Hello World", "root_path": request.scope.get("root_path")}
```

**Notes:**
- This setup assumes the proxy is **"stripping"** the **path prefix** on the fly before transmitting the request to the server, keeping your application convinced that it is being served at `/app`[1].
- Open the docs through the proxy URL (e.g. `/api/docs`). If you try the docs UI served by the server directly, without the path prefix in the URL, it won't work, because it expects to be accessed through the proxy.[3]

The docs I found use Traefik as the example proxy and don't cover Nginx-specific configuration. For the Nginx side, look in the Nginx documentation for how to strip a path prefix before forwarding requests. More details: https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/advanced/behind-a-proxy/
